                    ### Question

Participant A is strapped in a supine position on a bed turned upside down in a vertical orientation with his head towards the floor and his feet towards the ceiling. Participant B is strapped in a supine position on a bed turned downwards in a vertical orientation with his head towards the ceiling and his feet just about touching the floor. Participant C is strapped in a supine position on a bed in a horizontal orientation. Blood pressure readings are then taken at the level of the head, heart, and feet from all 3 participants. Which of these positions will have the lowest recorded blood pressure reading?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Participant A: at the level of the head
opb. Participant B: at the level of the feet
opc. Participant C: at the level of the heart

ope. Participant B: at the level of the head

For Participant A, with the head lower than the heart, increased hydrostatic pressure at the head results in higher blood pressure readings there. Conversely, the feet being higher than the heart leads to decreased hydrostatic pressure and lower blood pressure readings at the feet. For Participant B, with the feet lower than the heart, increased hydrostatic pressure results in higher blood pressure readings at the feet, while the head being higher than the heart results in decreased hydrostatic pressure and lower blood pressure readings at the head. Participant C, in a horizontal position, experiences equal hydrostatic pressure distribution, leading to normal blood pressure readings at the heart. Therefore, the lowest recorded blood pressure reading is expected at Participant B's head, where the head is higher than the heart, resulting in decreased hydrostatic pressure and lower blood pressure readings.
